examples.en: Add the oil once the frying pan has heated up.
The water heated up and began to steam.

examples.ko: 이 제품은 전자레인지에서 가열될 때 소리가 나요.
examples.en: This product makes a sound when it is heated in the microwave.

examples.ko: 오븐이 충분히 가열된 뒤에 빵을 넣어요.
examples.en: Put the bread in after the oven is fully heated.
The iron was heated and turned red.
The metal heats up too fast.

explain: 물이나 음식, 금속이 열을 받아 뜨거워질 때 써요. 열을 주는 쪽은 '가열하다'이고, 열이 지나치게 오른 상태는 '과열되다'라고 해요. 요리 설명서에는 '충분히 가열하세요' 같은 문장이 자주 나와요.
explain_en: Use it when water, food or metal receives heat and becomes hot. The one applying heat uses 가열하다, and too much heat is 과열되다. Cooking instructions often say 충분히 가열하세요.

examples.en: Even when failures kept piling up, I didn't give up.
The same question kept coming up, and I got tired of answering.
As accidents kept happening, people became anxious.
My body is tired because of the repeated overtime.
If this keeps happening, you lose trust.
After repeated efforts, I passed the exam.

explain: '거듭되다'는 같은 일이 연달아 이어지거나 쌓일 때 써요. '반복되다'보다 글 같은 말이고, 실패, 사고, 노력, 논란처럼 계속 겹치는 일에 잘 어울려요. '거듭되는', '거듭된'처럼 뒤의 명사를 꾸밀 때 특히 많이 써요.
explain_en: 거듭되다 is used when the same thing keeps happening one after another or piling up. It sounds more literary than 반복되다 and fits things that overlap again and again, such as failures, accidents, efforts, or controversies. It is especially common in the modifier forms 거듭되는 and 거듭된.

examples.en: Because of the exchange rate, stock prices plunged.

examples.ko: 이번 학기에 제 성적이 곤두박질쳐서 걱정이에요.
examples.en: My grades plummeted this semester, and I'm worried.

examples.ko: 자전거가 언덕 아래로 곤두박질치는 걸 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw the bicycle tumble headlong down the hill.
They told me to be careful so my popularity doesn't plunge.

examples.ko: 내일은 기온이 갑자기 곤두박질칠 거라고 해요.
examples.en: They say the temperature will suddenly plunge tomorrow.

examples.ko: 사고가 난 뒤에 회사 이미지가 곤두박질치고 말았어요.
examples.en: After the accident, the company's image ended up plummeting.

explain: 성적, 주가, 인기, 기온처럼 수치나 평가가 한꺼번에 크게 떨어질 때 자주 써요. 반대로 빠르게 오를 때는 '치솟다'를 써요. '폭락하다'보다 말하기에 편한 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is often used when numbers or ratings such as grades, stock prices, popularity or temperature drop sharply all at once. When they rise rapidly, the word is '치솟다'. It feels easier in speech than the formal '폭락하다'.

examples.ko: 정부의 정책이 급선회를 해서 모두 놀랐어요.
examples.en: The government's policy made a sudden turn, and everyone was surprised.

examples.ko: 운전자가 급선회를 하는 바람에 차가 크게 흔들렸어요.
examples.en: The driver turned sharply, so the car shook a lot.

examples.ko: 회사의 급선회로 해외 진출이 갑자기 결정됐어요.
examples.en: The company's sudden change of course led to a sudden decision to expand overseas.

examples.ko: 비행기의 급선회는 승객에게 위험할 수 있어요.
examples.en: A sharp turn of a plane can be dangerous for passengers.
The team members were very flustered by this sudden turn.
Thanks to the sharp turn, I barely avoided an accident.

explain: 차, 배, 비행기가 갑자기 방향을 바꿀 때도 쓰고, 정책이나 계획의 방향이 갑자기 달라질 때도 써요. 뉴스에서는 '정책 급선회'처럼 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is used when a car, ship or plane suddenly changes direction, and also when a policy or plan suddenly changes course. In the news it often appears like '정책 급선회'.

examples.en: I tripped on a stone and pitched forward.
I fell flat while running and hurt my knee.

examples.ko: 그 회사가 갑자기 꼬꾸라질 줄 몰랐어요.
examples.en: I didn't know that company would suddenly collapse.
I dozed off and almost fell face-first onto the desk.
The bicycle tipped over forward and the load spilled out.
The tree was toppled by the wind.

explain: '넘어지다'보다 앞으로 거꾸러지듯 쓰러지는 느낌이 강해요. '고꾸라지다'와 같은 말이에요. 사람이 넘어질 때뿐 아니라 회사나 주가가 갑자기 무너질 때도 비유로 써요.
explain_en: Compared with '넘어지다', it strongly suggests pitching forward headfirst. It means the same as '고꾸라지다'. Besides people falling, it is also used figuratively when a company or stock price suddenly collapses.

examples.en: A pickpocket snatched my bag.
The eagle snatched the fish in an instant.
The child snatched the phone out of my hand.
He snatched the ball and ran straight toward the goal.
Someone snatched my umbrella and ran off.

examples.ko: 그 팀이 경기 막판에 역전 기회를 낚아챘어요.
examples.en: That team seized the chance for a comeback late in the game.

explain: 갑자기 힘 있게 잡아서 가져가는 순간적인 동작이에요. '빼앗다'는 억지로 가져가는 뜻이 강하고, 낚아채다는 재빠른 손동작이 눈에 보이는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is a sudden, forceful grab that takes something away in a moment. '빼앗다' stresses taking by force, while 낚아채다 gives a vivid picture of a quick hand movement.

examples.ko: 폭풍 때문에 배가 난파 위기에 처했어요.
examples.en: The ship was in danger of being wrecked because of the storm.

examples.ko: 이 영화는 난파 사고에서 살아남은 사람들 이야기예요.
examples.en: This movie is about people who survived a shipwreck.
The rescue team searched for survivors at the wreck site.
The captain changed course to avoid being wrecked.

examples.ko: 오래전 난파로 바다 밑에 가라앉은 보물이 있대요.
examples.en: They say there is treasure that sank to the seabed in an old shipwreck.
The cause of the shipwreck was the fierce waves.

explain: 배가 부서지거나 가라앉는 일에 써요. 항공기 사고에는 보통 '추락'이라고 하고, 난파는 사고 뉴스나 모험 이야기에서 많이 보여요.
explain_en: It refers to a ship breaking up or sinking. For airplane accidents people usually say '추락' instead, and '난파' appears in accident news and adventure stories.

examples.en: I dawdled and missed the bus.

examples.ko: 정부의 늑장 대응 때문에 비판을 받았어요.
examples.en: The government was criticized for its slow response.
Don't dawdle first thing in the morning, hurry up.
My child dragged their feet and was late for school.

examples.ko: 늑장 출발 탓에 약속 시간에 늦었어요.
examples.en: Because of the late departure, I was late for the appointment.

examples.ko: 늑장 부릴 시간이 없어요, 빨리 와요.
examples.en: There's no time to dawdle, come quickly.

explain: '늑장을 부리다'라는 짝으로 가장 많이 쓰고, 뉴스에서는 '늑장 대응', '늑장 출동'처럼 나와요. '꾸물거리다'는 행동을 말하고, '늑장'은 해야 할 일을 일부러 늦추는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It is most often paired as '늑장을 부리다', and in the news it appears as '늑장 대응' or '늑장 출동'. '꾸물거리다' describes the action of dawdling, while '늑장' suggests putting off what you should be doing.

en: pouring cold water over one's back

examples.ko: 더운 여름날 아버지가 등목을 해 주셨어요.
examples.en: On a hot summer day, my father poured cold water over my back to cool me off.

examples.ko: 등목 좀 해 줄래요? 등이 너무 끈적해요.
examples.en: Can you pour some water over my back? It's so sticky.

examples.ko: 시골 할머니 댁 수돗가에서 한 등목이 제일 시원했어요.
examples.en: The back-rinse at the tap at my grandmother's country house was the most refreshing.

examples.ko: 등목을 하고 나니 더위가 싹 가셨어요.
examples.en: After the cold back-rinse, the heat was completely gone.

examples.ko: 형이 찬물로 제 등에 등목을 해 줬어요.
examples.en: My older brother poured cold water over my back.

examples.ko: 이렇게 더운 날에는 등목만 한 게 없어요.
examples.en: On a day this hot, nothing beats a cold rinse over the back.

explain: 엎드린 사람의 등에 찬물을 끼얹어 시원하게 하는 여름 풍경에서 쓰는 말로, '등목을 하다', '등목을 해 주다'라고 해요. 혼자 하기 어려워서 '등목 좀 해 줘'라고 부탁하기도 해요. '등물'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It belongs to the summer scene of someone bent over while cold water is poured over their back, and people say '등목을 하다' or '등목을 해 주다'. It is hard to do alone, so people ask '등목 좀 해 줘'. It is also called '등물'.

examples.ko: 가족들은 약간 거리를 두고 둘러서서 멀뚱히 바라보고 있었어요.
examples.en: The family stood around at a slight distance, just looking on blankly.

examples.ko: 모두 일하는데 혼자 멀뚱히 서 있기 민망해요.
examples.en: Everyone is working, so it's awkward to stand there doing nothing alone.

examples.ko: 동생이 멀뚱히 저를 보다가 갑자기 웃었어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling stared at me blankly and then suddenly laughed.

examples.ko: 멀뚱히 앉아만 있지 말고 이리 와서 도와요.
examples.en: Don't just sit there; come over and help.

examples.ko: 강아지가 멀뚱히 문 앞에서 기다리고 있어요.
examples.en: The puppy is waiting by the door, looking blank.

examples.ko: 선생님 말씀을 이해 못 해서 멀뚱히 칠판만 봤어요.
examples.en: I didn't understand the teacher, so I just stared blankly at the board.

explain: '멀뚱멀뚱'과 비슷하게 눈을 뜬 채 가만히 있는 모습이에요. '멀뚱히 서 있다/앉아 있다/바라보다'처럼 쓰고, 바쁜 곳에서 아무것도 안 하고 있는 사람을 은근히 나무라는 느낌이 들 때도 있어요.
explain_en: Like '멀뚱멀뚱', it describes staying still with eyes open and no reaction. It is used as '멀뚱히 서 있다/앉아 있다/바라보다'. It can also carry a mild reproach for someone doing nothing in a busy place.

examples.en: The banana got too mushy, so I don't want to eat it.
The tomatoes went soft in the fridge.
If you boil potatoes for a long time, they get soft.
Eat the peaches before they get soft.
I cut off the soft part of the pear and eat the rest.
I picked firm apples that don't get soft.

explain: 과일이나 채소가 시간이 지나거나 익어서 단단함이 없어질 때 써요. 기본형 '무르다'는 '르' 불규칙이라 '물러요', '물러졌어요'처럼 변해요. 반대말은 '단단하다'이고, 좋은 뜻으로 부드럽게 익었을 때보다 너무 말랑해서 상했다는 느낌이 있을 때 더 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is used when fruit or vegetables lose their firmness because of time or ripening. The base verb '무르다' is a '르' irregular, so it becomes '물러요' and '물러졌어요'. The opposite is '단단하다', and it often carries the feeling of being too soft or going bad.

examples.en: The old fallen leaf crumbled in my hand.

examples.ko: 쿠키를 가방에 넣었더니 다 바스러져 있었어요.
examples.en: I put the cookies in my bag, and they were all crumbled.
Dried petals crumble when you touch them.

examples.ko: 너무 오래된 종이라 손대면 바스러질 것 같아요.
examples.en: The paper is so old that it looks like it would crumble if touched.
The snack had crumbled, so it was awkward to eat.

examples.ko: 마른 흙이 바스러지는 느낌이 손에 남았어요.
examples.en: The feeling of dry soil crumbling stayed in my hand.

explain: '부서지다'보다 마르고 약한 것이 가루나 작은 조각으로 부서질 때 잘 어울려요. 낙엽, 과자, 마른 흙에 많이 쓰고, 더 큰 느낌의 말은 '부스러지다'예요.
explain_en: Compared with '부서지다', it fits dry, fragile things breaking into powder or small bits, such as leaves, snacks and dry soil. The bigger version is '부스러지다'.

examples.en: The baby kicked and struggled because it did not want to be held.

examples.ko: 물에 빠진 강아지가 필사적으로 발버둥 쳤어요.
examples.en: The puppy that fell into the water struggled desperately.

examples.ko: 아무리 발버둥 쳐도 상황은 나아지지 않았어요.
examples.en: No matter how much I struggled, the situation did not improve.
It was pitiful to see them struggling to survive.
His struggle ended up being in vain.

examples.ko: 남들보다 앞서 보려고 발버둥도 쳐 봤어요.
examples.en: I even struggled hard to try to get ahead of others.

explain: 원래는 누워서 발을 마구 구르는 동작인데, 힘든 상황에서 벗어나려고 애쓰는 모습에도 써요. 거의 '발버둥(을) 치다'로 쓰고, '노력하다'보다 절박하고 잘 안 풀리는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It originally means flailing and kicking your feet while lying down, and it is also used for desperate efforts to escape a hard situation. It is almost always used as '발버둥(을) 치다', and it feels more desperate and less successful than plain '노력하다'.

examples.ko: 아기가 안기기 싫은지 한참 버둥거리다가 울었어요.
examples.en: The baby squirmed for a while, as if not wanting to be held, and then cried.
The puppy that fell into the water flailed desperately.
Please don't kick your legs around while sitting on the chair.
The bug is flipped over and flailing its legs.

examples.ko: 혼자 버둥거려 봐도 문제가 해결되지 않아요.
examples.en: Even if I struggle on my own, the problem doesn't get solved.

examples.ko: 아이가 장난감을 사 달라며 바닥에서 버둥거려요.
examples.en: The child is thrashing on the floor, asking me to buy a toy.

explain: 팔다리를 크게 휘저으며 몸부림칠 때 쓰고, 어려운 상황에서 벗어나려고 애쓰는 모습에도 비유로 써요. 같은 뜻으로 '버둥대다'도 말해요. '발버둥을 치다'와 이어서 기억하면 쉬워요.
explain_en: It describes flailing your arms and legs, and also figuratively trying hard to get out of a difficult situation. '버둥대다' means the same. It helps to link it with '발버둥을 치다'.

examples.en: I overslept and rushed to school.
I hurriedly cleaned when I heard guests were coming.
After getting the call, I rushed to the hospital.
I hastily wrote the report the day before the deadline.

examples.ko: 비가 오자 사람들이 부랴부랴 빨래를 걷었어요.
examples.en: When it rained, people hurried to take in the laundry.
I left in such a rush that I forgot my wallet.

explain: 시간이 없어서 서두르는 모습인데, 미리 준비하지 못해서 급하게 한다는 느낌이 들어요. '빨리'는 속도만 말하고 '부랴부랴'는 당황한 느낌이 같이 있어요. 늘 '부랴부랴 + 동사'로 쓰고 형용사 앞에는 안 써요.
explain_en: It describes rushing because time is short, with a feeling of not being prepared. '빨리' only says fast; '부랴부랴' adds a flustered feel. It always goes before a verb, never before an adjective.

examples.en: I was late for the appointment, so I ran there in a hurry.
The moment I answered the call, I rushed out of the house.
My younger sibling came running in a hurry and told me the news.

examples.ko: 비가 오자 사람들이 부리나케 처마 밑으로 들어갔어요.
examples.en: When it started to rain, people scurried under the eaves.

examples.ko: 알람을 못 들어서 부리나케 준비하고 나왔어요.
examples.en: I didn't hear the alarm, so I got ready in a rush and came out.
When Mom called, the child answered right away.

explain: '급히'보다 허둥지둥 서두르는 모습이 눈에 보이는 말이에요. 주로 '뛰어가다', '달려오다', '나가다'처럼 움직임을 나타내는 동사와 같이 써요. 비슷한 말로 '서둘러서'가 있어요.
explain_en: Compared with '급히', it paints a picture of someone hurrying in a flustered way. It is mostly used with movement verbs like '뛰어가다', '달려오다' and '나가다'. A similar expression is '서둘러서'.

examples.ko: 옆자리 사람이 계속 부스럭대서 집중이 안 돼요.
examples.en: The person next to me keeps rustling, so I can't concentrate.
I heard someone rustling around all night.
The child rustled around under the blanket and then fell asleep.
Please don't rustle your bag in the movie theater.
A mouse was rustling in the ceiling.
What are you rustling around with in the room?

explain: '부스럭거리다'와 같은 뜻이고, '-대다'를 쓰면 말투가 조금 더 구어적이에요. 한 번이 아니라 소리가 계속 날 때 써요.
explain_en: It means the same as '부스럭거리다', and '-대다' sounds a bit more colloquial. Use it when the sound keeps going rather than happening once.

examples.en: The child clung to her mother's clothes and cried.
The moment I was about to fall, I grabbed the railing.

examples.ko: 그는 내 손을 부여잡고 고맙다고 했어요.
examples.en: He gripped my hand and said thank you.

examples.ko: 배를 부여잡은 채 웃느라 말을 못 했어요.
examples.en: I was clutching my stomach laughing, so I couldn't speak.

examples.ko: 바람이 세서 모자를 두 손으로 부여잡아야 했어요.
examples.en: The wind was strong, so I had to hold my hat with both hands.
Please don't grab the arm of someone who's trying to leave.

explain: '잡다'보다 세게 꼭 붙드는 느낌이고, 절박하거나 감정이 실린 장면에 많이 나와요. 말할 때는 '꽉 잡다'를 더 자주 써요.
explain_en: It feels stronger than '잡다', like holding on tightly, and it often appears in desperate or emotional scenes. In conversation people more often say '꽉 잡다'.

en: being half-asleep; being half-awake; being half-dreaming and half-awake

examples.ko: 어젯밤에 못 자서 아침 내내 비몽사몽이었어요.
examples.en: I couldn't sleep last night, so I was half asleep all morning.

examples.ko: 비몽사몽 중에 전화를 받아서 기억이 안 나요.
examples.en: I answered the phone half asleep, so I don't remember it.
I got up at dawn and went to work in a daze.
Driving while half asleep is dangerous.
I must still be half asleep, because I put my keys in the fridge.
I opened my eyes half asleep at the sound of the alarm.

explain: '비몽사몽이다', '비몽사몽 중에', '비몽사몽 상태'처럼 써요. 잠이 덜 깼거나 너무 졸려서 정신이 흐릿할 때 말해요. '잠결에'는 자는 동안 무심코 한 행동에 더 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It is used as '비몽사몽이다', '비몽사몽 중에' and '비몽사몽 상태'. You say it when you are not fully awake or so sleepy that your mind is hazy. '잠결에' fits better for something you did without thinking while sleeping.

examples.en: The village was stirred up when the rumor spread.
The students are buzzing about the exam results.
I could hear the theater buzzing.
Why is everybody so restless?
The office kept buzzing until just before the announcement.

examples.ko: 모두 술렁대서 수업을 시작할 수 없었어요.
examples.en: Everyone was so restless that we couldn't start class.

explain: '술렁거리다'와 같은 뜻이에요. 사람들이 웅성웅성하며 불안하거나 들떠 있을 때 써요. 더 짧은 '술렁이다'로도 말해요.
explain_en: It means the same as '술렁거리다'. It is used when people are murmuring, anxious or excited. The shorter '술렁이다' is also used.

examples.en: My younger sibling swiped one of my snacks.

examples.ko: 누가 내 펜을 슬쩍해 갔나 봐요.
examples.en: Someone seems to have swiped my pen.
I heard he got caught swiping an apple at the market.

examples.ko: 친구 지우개를 슬쩍한 적이 있어서 아직도 미안해요.
examples.en: I once swiped a friend's eraser, and I still feel sorry.
You must not swipe other people's things.
I almost swiped a candy in the store, but I held back.

explain: '훔치다'보다 가볍고 구어적이라 장난처럼 들려요. 그래서 진짜 도둑질을 말할 때는 조심해서 써요. 부사 '슬쩍'은 몰래 살짝 한다는 느낌으로 훨씬 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is lighter and more colloquial than 훔치다 and can sound playful, so be careful using it for real theft. The adverb 슬쩍, meaning quietly and lightly, is much more common.

examples.ko: 빚에 쫓기던 그 가족은 어느 날 야반도주를 했어요.
examples.en: The family, chased by debt, fled in the night one day.

examples.ko: 드라마에서 두 사람이 야반도주하는 장면이 나왔어요.
examples.en: There was a scene in the drama where the two run away in the night.

examples.ko: 가게 주인이 월급도 안 주고 야반도주했대요.
examples.en: I heard the shop owner skipped town at night without even paying wages.
My parents opposed it so strongly that I even thought about eloping in the night.

examples.ko: 이사 간 줄 알았는데 야반도주였다는 소문이 돌았어요.
examples.en: I thought they had moved, but a rumor went around that they had fled in the night.

examples.ko: 월세를 못 내서 야반도주한 사람이 있었어요.
examples.en: There was someone who couldn't pay the rent and fled in the night.

explain: 밤에 몰래 도망치는 모습을 말해요. 빚이나 반대 때문에 몰래 떠나는 이야기에 자주 나오고, 보통 '야반도주하다'로 말해요. 그냥 '도망가다'보다 한밤에 아무도 모르게 떠난다는 느낌이 강해요.
explain_en: It describes secretly running away in the middle of the night. It often appears in stories about debts or opposition from family, and people usually say '야반도주하다'. Compared with plain '도망가다', it strongly suggests slipping away at night where nobody notices.

examples.en: Riding the momentum of their victory, they reached the final.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 여세를 몰아서 다음 경기도 이겼어요.
examples.en: Our team kept the momentum and won the next game too.

examples.ko: 이 여세로 올해 목표를 이루고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to achieve this year's goal riding this momentum.
That team has tremendous momentum from its winning streak.

examples.ko: 여세를 몰아 숙제를 끝까지 다 했어요.
examples.en: I kept up the momentum and finished all my homework.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 인기 여세를 이어서 새 앨범을 냈어요.
examples.en: The singer kept up her popularity and released a new album.

explain: '여세를 몰아(서)' 모양으로 거의 쓰여서, 좋은 일이 있은 뒤의 기세를 타고 다음 일을 밀어붙인다는 뜻이에요. 대체로 승리나 성공처럼 긍정적인 흐름에 써요.

phrases.example: 어제 이긴 여세를 몰아 오늘도 이겼어요.
phrases.en: Riding yesterday's win, we won again today.
phrases.nuance_ko: '몰다'의 본래 뜻과 달리, 좋은 기세를 놓치지 않고 계속 이어 간다는 비유로 굳은 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Unlike the original sense of '몰다' (to drive), this is a set figurative phrase for keeping a good momentum going.

explain_en: It is used almost entirely as '여세를 몰아(서)', meaning to ride the energy after something good and push on to the next thing. It usually applies to positive flows such as victory or success.

en: keep doing one after another; fire off repeatedly

examples.ko: 그 선수는 경기 중에 실수를 연발했어요.
examples.en: That player made one mistake after another during the game.
The child fired off questions one after another, and I was busy answering.

examples.ko: 코미디언이 농담을 연발하자 관객이 크게 웃었어요.
examples.en: When the comedian kept cracking jokes, the audience laughed loudly.
I was nervous and ended up making slip after slip.
We admired the night view, exclaiming again and again.
If you keep yawning repeatedly, it's a sign you're sleepy.

explain: 말이나 실수, 행동을 잇따라 계속 한다는 뜻이에요. '실수·농담·질문·감탄사를 연발하다'처럼 목적어를 받아요. '계속하다'보다 짧은 간격으로 연달아 나온다는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It means doing or saying something one after another without a pause. It takes an object, as in '실수·농담·질문·감탄사를 연발하다'. Compared with '계속하다', it feels like things come out in quick succession.

examples.ko: 권한을 오용하면 큰 책임을 져야 해요.
examples.en: If you misuse your authority, you have to take big responsibility.
People often misuse this word.

examples.ko: 약을 오용해서 병원에 간 적이 있어요.
examples.en: I once went to the hospital because I misused medicine.
They promised not to misuse personal information.

examples.ko: 이 표현을 오용한 광고가 논란이 됐어요.
examples.en: An ad that misused this expression caused controversy.
A rumor went around that public funds had been misused.

explain: '남용하다'는 너무 많이 쓴다는 쪽이고 '악용하다'는 나쁜 목적으로 쓴다는 쪽이에요. '오용하다'는 알맞지 않은 방식으로 잘못 쓴다는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: '남용하다' leans toward using too much, and '악용하다' toward using for a bad purpose. '오용하다' feels like using something in the wrong, unsuitable way.

examples.ko: 어제 경기에서 우리 팀이 완패를 당했어요.
examples.en: Our team suffered a crushing defeat in yesterday's game.
It was a total loss, but the players did their best to the end.

examples.ko: 이번 대회는 우리 팀의 완패로 끝났어요.
examples.en: This tournament ended in a complete defeat for our team.

examples.ko: 완패의 원인을 분석해서 다음엔 이길 거예요.
examples.en: We'll analyze why we lost so badly and win next time.
Everyone was silent at the result of a total defeat.

examples.ko: 지난번 완패를 잊지 못하고 열심히 연습했어요.
examples.en: We couldn't forget the last crushing defeat, so we practiced hard.

explain: 반대말은 '완승'이고, 크게 지는 걸 '대패'라고도 해요. '완패를 당하다', '완패로 끝나다'처럼 쓰고, 행동으로 말할 때는 '완패하다'를 써요.
explain_en: The opposite is '완승', and losing big is also called '대패'. It is used in '완패를 당하다' and '완패로 끝나다', and as an action you say '완패하다'.

examples.en: The bag was small, but I crammed the clothes in anyway.
I was in a hurry, so I stuffed bread into my mouth and ran out.

examples.ko: 짐을 다 욱여넣어도 가방이 안 닫혀요.
examples.en: Even if I cram all the stuff in, the bag won't close.
Don't cram the papers into the drawer; organize them.
Lunch break was short, so I shoveled my food down.

examples.ko: 좁은 트렁크에 짐을 욱여넣느라 땀이 났어요.
examples.en: I broke a sweat cramming the luggage into the small trunk.

explain: '넣다'와 달리 좁은 곳에 억지로 밀어 넣는 느낌이 강해요. 짐이나 옷뿐 아니라 음식을 입에 급하게 넣을 때도 써요. 말할 때는 '쑤셔 넣다'도 비슷하게 쓰는데, 그쪽이 좀 더 거칠게 들려요.
explain_en: Unlike plain '넣다', it carries a strong sense of forcing things into a tight space. It works for luggage and clothes, and also for hurriedly stuffing food into your mouth. In speech '쑤셔 넣다' is similar, but it sounds a bit rougher.

examples.en: He flinched at the sudden question.

examples.ko: 개가 짖자 아이가 움찔해서 엄마 뒤에 숨었어요.
examples.en: When the dog barked, the child flinched and hid behind her mom.

examples.ko: 제가 큰 소리로 말하니까 동생이 움찔하더라고요.
examples.en: When I spoke loudly, my younger sibling flinched.

examples.ko: 차가운 물이 닿자 살짝 움찔하는 게 보였어요.
examples.en: I saw him flinch slightly when the cold water touched him.

examples.ko: 무서운 장면이 나올 때마다 저도 모르게 움찔해요.
examples.en: Every time a scary scene comes on, I flinch without realizing it.

examples.ko: 그는 비난을 받아도 전혀 움찔하지 않고 끝까지 말했어요.
examples.en: Even when criticized, he didn't flinch at all and spoke to the end.

explain: '놀라다'는 마음의 반응이고, '움찔하다'는 놀라거나 겁이 나서 몸이 순간 움츠러드는 것을 말해요. '말에 움찔하다'처럼 기가 죽는 상황에도 써요. 반대로는 '움찔도 하지 않다'라고 해요.
explain_en: '놀라다' is about the mind being startled, while '움찔하다' is the body shrinking back for a moment from surprise or fear. It also works when someone is cowed by words, as in '말에 움찔하다'. For the opposite you can say '움찔도 하지 않다' (not even flinch).

examples.en: He got angry and twisted up his face.
The impact crumpled the front of the car.
The child put on a tearful look and screwed up his expression.
The pain twisted his smile out of shape.

examples.ko: 뜨거운 열이 플라스틱 통을 일그러뜨려서 못 쓰게 됐어요.
examples.en: The intense heat warped the plastic container, so it became unusable.

examples.ko: 그 경험이 아이들의 순수한 마음을 일그러뜨리지 않았으면 좋겠어요.
examples.en: I hope that experience doesn't warp the children's innocent hearts.

explain: '일그러지다'와 짝이에요. 얼굴이 일그러지다 / 얼굴을 일그러뜨리다처럼 목적어가 있으면 '-뜨리다'를 써요. '일그러트리다'로도 쓰고, 얼굴에 쓰면 보통 아프거나 화난 표정이에요.
explain_en: It is the transitive partner of '일그러지다'. Compare 얼굴이 일그러지다 with 얼굴을 일그러뜨리다; with an object you use '-뜨리다'. '일그러트리다' is also used, and with a face it usually means a pained or angry expression.

examples.ko: 두 나라는 일촉즉발의 위기에 놓여 있어요.
examples.en: The two countries are in a crisis that could explode at any moment.

examples.ko: 두 사람의 싸움이 일촉즉발 상황까지 갔어요.
examples.en: The two people's fight went to the brink of exploding.
The border area is still a tinderbox.
It was on the verge of blowing up, yet nobody stopped them.
The conflict that was heading to the breaking point was resolved through talking.
The tense atmosphere that was about to blow was eased by laughter.

explain: 조금만 건드려도 터질 것처럼 위험한 상황을 말해요. 전쟁, 갈등, 분위기에 쓰고 '일촉즉발의 위기/상황'으로 뉴스에서 많이 봐요. 가볍게 말할 때는 '아슬아슬하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It describes a situation so dangerous that the slightest touch could make it explode. It is used for war, conflict and atmosphere, and seen in the news as '일촉즉발의 위기/상황'. For lighter talk, people say '아슬아슬하다'.
